why: The change is fully specified, but it rebuilds the admin's session client by hand, copying @supabase/ssr's internals (storage key, cookie encoding, pkce, refresh flags). The two-way session test and the signed-in e2e catch a wrong cookie name or encoding. They do not catch a refresh that fails after an hour (the stand-in sessions are short and the e2e never idles past a token's life), or an option left out of supabase-js's own auth set-up (lock, fetch). Commit 2 is also stale against step 0.9, which already moves the nine upload files to a lazy uploadToSignedUrl() helper.
harm_if_wrong: A hand-built auth client that writes or refreshes the session cookie slightly differently from the server's createServerClient would sign staff out after an hour, or loop them through SessionRecovery, in production, and no automated check before the push would see it.
make_it_cheaper: Import publicEnv from '@/lib/public-env' (not '@/lib/env'), rewrite commit 2 against what step 0.9 leaves (signed-upload.ts already loads the client by import(), so the scan's starting list is empty), and add a unit test that drives a token refresh with fake timers and checks the refreshed cookie can be read by createServerClient's storage; then commit 2 is cheap and commit 1 stays review only for being sign-in.
brief_problems: auth-client.ts is told to read publicEnv() from '@/lib/env'; after step 0.9 that module still builds the server's zod schema at its top, so importing it into the idle client would bring zod back into every admin screen. Step 0.9 made '@/lib/public-env' for exactly this.

Commit 2 lists nine files that import '@/lib/supabase/client' statically 'on 12 November' and tells the model to convert each to an inline import(); step 0.9 (a dependency) already replaced all nine with uploadToSignedUrl() from src/lib/supabase/signed-upload.ts, so the list and the edits no longer match the code.

The AuthClient options are copied by hand from createBrowserClient and _initSupabaseAuthClient; the brief lists some but says 'copy their arguments exactly', leaving the model to decide whether supabase-js's lock, fetch and other auth defaults also apply.
